title: Your immune defenses

infection.q: One of the main symptoms of low immunoglobulin levels is frequent infections, especially repeated infections from the same germ.

signs.q: One pneumonia per year for more than 1 year
Respiratory infections, such as pneumonia and bronchitis.

It is important to remember that none of the results from a CBC with differential can diagnose PI alone.
In addition, CBC results within the reference ranges do not rule out PI either.
If a healthcare provider thinks someone might have an antibody deficiency, the first laboratory test they order is called a serum immunoglobulin (Ig) test
This test measures the levels of IgG, IgA, and IgM antibodies in the person’s blood.
The next test for antibody deficiencies is called a vaccine challenge.
Healthcare providers might order additional tests that measure B cells in a person’s blood if they suspect the person has an antibody deficiency.
If a healthcare provider thinks someone has a complement system problem, they may order an initial test called the total hemolytic complement assay (CH50).
An immunoglobulins blood test alone cannot diagnose any conditions.
Usually, a healthcare provider will confirm low or high values from a single serum Ig test by repeating the test several weeks later.
Note that vaccine challenge responses should be interpreted by a healthcare provider who sees individuals with PI on a regular basis, like a clinical immunologist.
